output.summary: KEP-5474 proposes a CRI-based, opt-in field (CgroupOptions in the Pod SecurityContext) to let containers mount cgroups writable. The KEP is now implementable at alpha, after the design was narrowed to a CRI-level contract with kubelet-set Pod-level descendant and depth limits.
output.rationale: Unprivileged containers have read-only cgroupfs by default, which blocks workloads that manage their own sub-cgroups. Reviewers pushed for a runtime-agnostic CRI contract, for relying on cgroup namespaces and nsdelegate rather than file permissions, and for bounding cgroup creation (cgroup.max.descendants / cgroup.max.depth) to avoid kernel DoS. The SIG-Node meeting of 2026-05-13 preferred kubelet setting Pod-level limits over adding per-container fields to the CRI, and the maintainer later agreed to that approach.

alternatives.option: Model writable cgroups as a new Cgroup volume type with a readOnly field
alternatives.why_not: Chrishenzie argued it could confuse users about mount points and that it is closer to readOnlyRootFilesystem or procMount; pmengelbert argued for the volume model, so the thread did not settle it in the sources.

alternatives.option: Make writable cgroups the default for Guaranteed QoS pods or for all containers
alternatives.why_not: Open questions were raised about default behavior, cgroup v1 nodes, and the container runtime's read-only default; the sources do not record a final default decision beyond the Guaranteed-only requirement.

alternatives.option: Set cgroup.max.descendants and cgroup.max.depth via the Pod spec (resource limits) or per-container CRI fields
alternatives.why_not: The 2026-05-13 SIG-Node discussion preferred kubelet-set Pod-level defaults because it was simpler and avoided expanding the CRI API until a use case appears.

alternatives.option: Use NRI as the mechanism instead of a built-in K8s feature
alternatives.why_not: dchen1107 notes an NRI solution exists, but SIG-Node agreed there are advantages to having this visibility in Kubernetes; NRI is to be documented as an alternative consideration.

evidence.quote: It was suggested we make it kubelet's responsibility to set descendants and depth at the Pod-level rather than add this to the CRI API (at least for now).
I think we do not want to introduce these changes yet, and instead have kubelet set sane defaults for max descendents and depth on the Pod-level cgroup.
We discussed it at SIG Node and agreed there are much advantages to have this visibility to K8s.
I have addressed the comments and have removed specific runtime references.
This mount option makes it so that: > - Writes to controller interface files in the root directory of the namespace will fail with the error EPERM.
